questions.stem: On a distance-time graph, what does a horizontal line represent?
questions.explanation: A horizontal line on a distance-time graph means the distance is not changing with time, so the object is stationary.

questions.stem: What does the gradient of a distance-time graph represent?
questions.explanation: The gradient (slope) of a distance-time graph equals the speed, since gradient = change in distance / change in time.

questions.stem: On a distance-time graph, a straight diagonal line with a steep gradient indicates:
questions.explanation: A straight diagonal line means constant speed. A steeper gradient means a faster speed, because more distance is covered in the same time.

questions.stem: What does a curved line on a distance-time graph indicate?

options.text: The object is moving at constant speed
The speed is changing (the object is accelerating or decelerating)

questions.explanation: A curved line means the gradient is changing, which means the speed is changing. The object is either accelerating or decelerating.

questions.stem: An object travels 60 metres in 10 seconds at constant speed. What is the gradient of its distance-time graph?
questions.explanation: Gradient = change in distance / change in time = 60 m / 10 s = 6 m/s.

questions.stem: How do you find the instantaneous speed from a curved distance-time graph?

options.text: Read the distance value directly from the graph
Draw a tangent to the curve at that point and find its gradient
Calculate total distance divided by total time
Find the area under the curve

questions.explanation: To find instantaneous speed from a curve, draw a tangent to the curve at the point of interest and calculate the gradient of that tangent line.

questions.stem: On a distance-time graph, can the line ever go downward?

options.text: No, because distance can only increase or stay the same
Yes, when the object moves backwards

questions.explanation: Distance is a scalar that always increases or stays the same -- you cannot un-travel distance. A displacement-time graph, however, can go downward.
